newsitem.title: FRANCE: Best French wheat bid for 41,000 tonnes - trade.
newsitem.headline: Best French wheat bid for 41,000 tonnes - trade.

text.p: The first tranche of European Union wheat subsidies sought through France on Thursday was for 41,000 tonnes at 5.31 Ecus per tonne, traders said.
The lowest refund bid implies the highest world price, which traders estimated at around $166 per tonne.
Going further up the subsidy scale, cumulative bids for refunds up to six Ecus per tonne were for 105,000 tonnes.
Traders said bids up to and including refunds of 6.5 Ecus were for an estimated total of 135,000 tonnes.
Bids up to seven Ecus were for 195,000 tonnes and those up to 7.5 Ecus were for 224,000 tonne.
Eight Ecus covered a cumulative volume just slightly higher at 226,500 tonnes, while bids up to nine Ecus covered 311,000.
Cereals office ONIC does not comment on the breakdown but earlier said the total range of bids was for 325,500 tonnes at between 5.31 and 11.95 Ecus per tonne.
